title: Jelly Roll Morton: Winin' Boy and his clothes
summary: Ory describes Morton's walk, silk shirts, diamonds and pimping.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Remembering Jelly Roll Morton: the man, the band

blocks.x: Kid Ori, April 20th, 1957, Reel 4. Did you know General from New Orleans? Oh, yeah.
Well, the only General never crossed Canal Street as a musician to play. Yeah.
Yeah. But you hadn't played with him in New Orleans, you just knew him. No.
Yeah. No. I'd be dressed in the... His name was Winning Boy. That's what it is. Winning Boy, huh? Yeah. He used to wine when he walked, you know. You know, I kind of called him.
Oh, yeah? Yeah. Is that why they called him Winning Boy? Yeah. I never knew why they called him Winning Boy. How do you know?

What was the idea of that? Walking that way? Well, they called him Winning Boy. The women like to be there. Used to like that. A real sharp walk? Yeah. Yeah, sharp walk. Showing off what he had to offer. Put the hat down and one suspended down in the shirt sleeve or on. That's the one. Ha! Ha!

How'd jelly dress in those days? Oh, just nice. What kind of clothes? Oh, tight leg trousers and this and style, you know. Uh-huh. High roller hats. Uh-huh. What kind of shoes? Button shoes. Button shoes. Sharp man. Sharp man. Ha! Ha! What kind of shirts do you wear with? Silk shirts.
Was he a pimp? Huh? Was he, did you do a little pimping on the side?
He was a kind of a pimple. He was, huh?
Yeah, yeah, yeah, yeah. Did he have girls working for him?
I don't know. He asked me a little too early. Ha! Ha! Ha! Well, he worked all right.
But he sure acquired those diamonds there. Yeah.
He was all right. He was, he did all right. Was he nice to you? Oh, he was good. Were you good friends? Oh, yeah.
